item.description:
Wang, J., Huang, Y.
This paper presents a scalable, nonparametric approach to estimating point-wise price elasticities designed for real-time pricing decisions. A key challenge in these settings is correcting for price endogeneity while remaining computationally efficient. This task is challenging because the number of covariance elements grows quickly with the number of assets, whereas the available time-series observations are limited and noisy. In order to find a desired treatment plan, a decision maker must balance the various objectives as well as the level of robustness towards uncertainty against each other. Sequential zone picking systems provide high throughput and flexibility. Under heavy load they are vulnerable to congestion and blocking when conveyor merges, staffing fluctuations, heterogeneous picking speeds, and inventory shortfalls interact. Various approaches have been suggested to transform such nonsmooth operators equivalently into systems of constraints. item.title: Spoofing and Manipulating Order Books with Learning Algorithms
item.description:
Cartea, A., Chang, P., Garcia Arenas, G.
We propose a dynamic model of the limit order book to derive conditions to test whether it is optimal to manipulate the order book. Our results show that as a market maker becomes more tolerant to bearing inventory risk, optimal strategies that manipulate the book occur more frequently. item.description:
Schneeberger, A., Krupka, E.
What determines whether someone complies with a social norm? The social identity approach offers a mechanism for norm compliance: A person who feels similar to a group identifies more with that group and, in turn, complies with the group’s norms. Using an experiment, we test whether similarity in values increases identification and adherence to a group rule. item.title: Screening, Investment Incentives, and the Welfare Trade-Offs of Privacy
item.description:
Dosis, A., Rothschild, C.
This paper studies how information disclosure affects investment incentives and contracting efficiency. We analyze a class of principal-agent models in which information helps the principal screen the agent but also facilitates surplus appropriation, thereby weakening the agent’s incentive to invest before contracting. item.description:
Gurun, U., Liu, Z., Xiao, S.
The rising dominance of superplatforms raises concerns about conflicts of interest and externalities on innovation, because they act as both marketplace gatekeepers and strategic investors. Studying Google’s dual role via Google Ventures (GV) and the Android marketplace, we find Google-backed startups receive 115% more reviews, 12% higher ratings, and 77% fewer bug complaints than their iOS counterparts—despite no major app updates. item.description:
Spiller, S.
Measures of overconfidence are used both to assess biases in people’s beliefs regarding their own abilities and to identify correlates of those biases. Proposed correlates of overconfidence include narcissism, social status, (low) task anxiety, savings, planning, and many more. In this work we address the problem of optimal estimating the position of each agent in a network from relative noisy vectorial distances with its neighbors. item.description:

Semimartingale optimal transport arises in a wide range of applications, including mathematical finance and flow-based generative models. A recurring computational challenge is that the dual energy functional is often poorly conditioned with respect to the dual potential, leading to slow convergence of gradient descent algorithms. item.description:
Yanlin Li, Ganzhao Yuan
We propose NABLA, a noise-adaptive blockwise left-right preconditioning algorithm for mini-batch stochastic nonconvex optimization. NABLA combines an exponential moving average of stochastic gradients with block-diagonal row and column preconditioners constructed from matrix-valued second-moment statistics. Konstantinos Emmanouilidis, Ziqing Xu, Salma Tarmoun, Lachlan MacDonald, Rene Vidal
Stochastic Gradient Descent lies at the core of modern machine learning. However its classical analysis typically restricts the stepsize to be below a curvature-dependent stability threshold. Recent developments in deterministic optimization have challenged this paradigm, showing that suitably chosen large stepsizes can not only preserve convergence, but also accelerate Gradient Descent (GD). Emir Cem Gezer, Ozan Kaya, Ingrid B. Utne, Roger Skjetne

This paper presents a risk-informed Rapidly Exploring Random Tree Star (RRT*) path planner that integrates a Bayesian Belief Network (BBN) as an online risk model. Under assumptions on the existence of a data set and the Lipschitz continuity of the unknown part {of the dynamics}, an uncertainty set is constructed and used to adapt the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation towards a data-driven formulation. Martin Staadecker, Patricia Hidalgo-Gonzalez
Researchers and industry practitioners are constructing increasingly large optimization models to tackle problems in fields such as manufacturing, logistics, and energy systems planning. As the performance of solvers like Gurobi keeps improving, the performance of modeling frameworks like gurobipy which let users interact with solvers is increasingly becoming a bottleneck. item.description:

The classical traffic assignment problem determines the equilibrium flows on a congested network with many infinitesimal users who choose paths to minimize their own travel times. Travelers care about cost (including tolls) as well as time, and different travelers put different weights on these two criteria. item.description:
Thomas Berger
The stored energy and the electron density of a burning tokamak plasma must be kept inside prescribed bands, with the auxiliary heating power and the fuelling rate as actuators. For the standard zero-dimensional burn model with a dynamic confinement closure we show that this two-actuator configuration has vector relative degree $(2,1)$, independently of the confinement parameters. item.description:
Atefeh Hemmati Golsefidi, David Pisinger
One of the most common models for handling uncertainty is two-stage stochastic programming. Choosing the right number of scenarios is a trade-off between the uncertainty that can be represented and computational cost. item.description:

This paper studies the observability decomposition of Boolean networks (BNs) and Boolean control networks (BCNs) in the semi-tensor product framework. We characterize when a BN admits an observability decomposition in terms of the equivalence classes induced by indistinguishability. Proximal Stochastic Gradient Descent minimizes the sum of an $L$-smooth convex function $f$, known through unbiased stochastic gradients of bounded variance, and a nonsmooth convex function $R$, known through its proximity operator. item.description:

Let $φ$ be a proper piecewise linear-quadratic (PLQ) function whose domain meets the unit sphere $\mathcal{S}$. item.title: Fractional minimality of the Simons cone for $s$ close to $1$
item.description:
Matteo Novaga, Emanuele Paolini
We prove that the Simons cone in $\mathbb R^8$ minimizes the fractional perimeter $P_s$, under compact perturbations, whenever $s$ is sufficiently close to $1$.

item.description:

item.description:

item.title: On Semilocal Convergence of a Semismooth* Newton Method
item.description:
Tomáš Roubal
We give conditions under which the semismooth$^*$ Newton method solves $0\in F(x)$ from a given initial point. At each step, we bound the distance from the corrected point $(x_{k+1},0)$ to the graph of $F$ by a function of the correction length. We also bound $\|A^{-1}B\|$ uniformly over the selected coderivative pairs $(A,B)$. Together, these bounds give a test on the initial graph residual and the radius of a prescribed ball. If the test holds, the iterates converge to a solution in that ball.

item.description:

In this paper, we consider a four-stage variant of robust optimization with cost uncertainty described by the budget uncertainty polytope, known as decision-dependent information discovery (DDID). In this problem, the decision maker first queries a subset of the cost coefficients. item.description:

In contextual stochastic optimization, integrated learning trains conditional models on operational loss, but repeatedly solving stochastic programs with many scenarios is costly. item.description:
Zhi Xu, Ran Dai
This paper presents a learning-based Koopman framework for solving constrained nonlinear optimal control problems. Despite significant advances in Koopman-based modeling and control, challenges remain in achieving accurate representations of controlled nonlinear dynamics and constraints while maintaining computational efficiency for optimal control. item.description:

item.description:

We study gradient-based search for a class of convex simulation optimization problems with gradients estimated from noisy outputs. With independent outputs, the optimal classical convergence rate for the expected objective gap is of order $O(N^{-2/3})$, where $N$ is the query budget. item.description:
Yida Xu, Baichuan Mo, Zhengzhong Ricky You, Yuan Zhou, Hao Yi Ong et al.
Ride-hailing platforms use driver-facing surge maps to rebalance spatial supply by offering zone-level bonuses. These bonuses can reshape supply by inducing nearby drivers to relocate and encouraging latent drivers to become dispatchable, but both responses are voluntary. item.description:

item.description:

item.description:

We propose a deterministic stepsize rule for gradient descent on a lower-bounded nonconvex function with Lipschitz-continuous gradient and Hessian. Classical analysis shows that a fixed stepsize guarantees a decrease of order $\varepsilon^2/L$ per update. item.description:
